A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Goal Force work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching retained results across renamed scenes.

before.justification: v1 reports original human preference studies, visual-planning success rates, diversity measurements, and mass-conditioned collision experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports an expanded human study, additional planning results in Table 5, and qualitative ablation findings in Section 7.3.

M1.justification: The three-channel force/mass representation, causal masking strategy, Wan2.2 ControlNet architecture, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 7.3 tests ablated variants without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Constrained-planning coverage expands beyond the six tabulated domino, pool, and duck scenes to household and tabletop environments, including paper balls, coffee cups, curling stones, and nine tool-use scenarios with distractors (Table 5 and Figure 7). The synthetic training datasets and four human-study task categories remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: zero-shot and fine-tuned text-only baselines in Table 1; PhysGen, PhysDreamer, Force Prompting, and Tora in Figure 4; and the same benchmark-specific comparator sets in Table 4. Citation consolidation does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 expands the reported benchmark from 25 to 75 scenes and the human study from 10 to 40 participants. Section 7.3 adds training-channel masking and prompt-variation controls. The three preference criteria, 2AFC design, and planning evaluation using 50 generated videos per scene with artifact filtering remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 7.3 examines three central conditioning choices: replacing the mass channel with text, removing the direct-force channel during training, and varying action wording or specifying its source. These add component and prompt-sensitivity analyses absent from v1, although their findings are reported qualitatively without numerical ablation tables.

E5.justification: The 26 diversity seeds, 15 videos per mass combination, and point-estimate reporting remain unchanged. Neither version provides confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Increasing human participants changes evaluation sample size, not repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the preference results under the expanded evaluation: force-adherence preference over zero-shot text changes from 57% to 73.4% for two-object collisions and from 96.7% to 74.5% for tool-object interaction. These are not same-setting performance changes. Table 5 adds 16 numerical planning entries while retaining all six earlier result triples under revised scene labels. Section 7.3 adds qualitative ablation findings; Table 3, Table 4, and Figure 6 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The control-tensor definition, relative force/mass formulation, and diversity metric in Equation 1 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: goal-conditioned causal planning, implicit physics simulation without an inference-time simulator, and generalization from synthetic primitives to complex interactions. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 newly explains that unspecified action sources can produce an invisible force through the pretrained prior. It clarifies the distinction between specifying a high-level interaction source and specifying low-level dynamics, and motivates source specification for robotics. This adds a substantive applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Section 7.3 supplies concrete prompt alternatives and identifies training-time channel masking and text-based mass replacement for the new ablations. These are limited reproducibility additions; training hyperparameters, hardware, synthetic-data recipes, and code/data release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference count falls from 71 to 67 by consolidating duplicate entries for Learning to Act from Actionless Videos, Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines, PhysCtrl, and Tora. The cited research works and substantive positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized copyedits, removes a repetitive diversity paragraph, updates planning-result cross-references, and adds Section 7.3 without reorganizing the main narrative. Section 4.2 also reverses the cause/effect parentheticals, introducing an inconsistency with the unchanged definitions in Section 3.1.

P2.justification: v2 adds the complete planning-results Table 5 and the 22-scene visualization in Figure 7. Table 2 becomes a selected-results display, with earlier entries retained in the appendix. These are localized presentation additions; Figures 1–6 and the overall document layout remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The broader constrained-planning tests and expanded human comparison strengthen support for generalization, while Table 5 and Figure 7 make the evaluation easier to inspect. Section 7.3 adds useful component checks and identifies an invisible-force failure condition. The gains are limited by unquantified ablations and a new cause/effect terminology inconsistency in Section 4.2, but overall evidential support and transparency improve.
